services.name: cloudfront-cdn
services.purpose: Deliver website content via CDN with HTTPS

services.name: acm-certificate
services.purpose: Provide TLS certificate for the CDN

services.name: route53-dns
services.purpose: Map custom domain to the CloudFront distribution

services.name: s3-website-iam
services.purpose: Allow CloudFront to read objects from the S3 bucket

dependencies.description: CloudFront uses the S3 bucket as its origin
CloudFront uses the ACM certificate for HTTPS
Route53 creates an alias record that points to the CloudFront distribution
IAM policy grants CloudFront read access to the S3 bucket

ingress: HTTPS (443) from any IP address to CloudFront distribution
network.notes: Static website is served publicly via CloudFront; the S3 bucket is configured for private access, allowing only CloudFront to read objects.

ambiguities.detail: Deploying all resources in the US East (N. Virginia) region because no region was specified.
Using a placeholder domain name; replace with the actual marketing site domain.
ACM certificate will be validated via DNS records as no validation method was given.
S3 bucket name follows a lowercase slug pattern; replace with the desired unique bucket name.
Limiting CloudFront edge locations to US, Canada, and Europe to control cost.
Using AWS's recommended TLS 1.2 security policy for the CDN.
The plan assumes the hosted zone is present; otherwise one must be created.
ambiguities.assumption: A Route53 public hosted zone already exists for the domain

ambiguities.detail: CloudFront access logs will be written to a separate S3 bucket (not defined) to aid monitoring.
Using CloudFront's default cache TTL settings because no custom caching rules were specified.
No AWS WAF protection is added as the description did not mention security beyond HTTPS.
